eli5.text: The coding assistant that works behind the scenes on complex tasks now relies on a different underlying service to generate code. Two additional services it can call upon have been added to the list it keeps ready in memory for faster reuse. If you watched the assistant do its work, you wouldn't see a new button or setting; the change is in which helper it listens to and which helpers it pre-warms, so responses come from a different source than before.

ai.title: Document init-agents command and custom tool definitions
ai.summary: README.md adds documentation for the `codebuff init-agents` command and expands details on custom agent creation. The update clarifies that agents can define tools, spawn subagents, and use prompts, alongside existing TypeScript generator support. A `customToolDefinitions` field is added to the SDK example code. The 'Why choose Codebuff' section reorders points and adds a note about reusing published agents via MCP-like composition.

eli5.text: If you build your own specialized assistants, running a single setup command now generates a starter project with examples for adding custom tools, sub-agents, and prompts. The guide also gained a new field for registering those custom tools, plus clearer wording and reordered selling points that emphasize building advanced workflows and reusing already-published assistants. Everything below still works as before for the broader user base; only the custom-assistant creation flow was changed.
